data.description:
# Outbound status changes silently fail on any workflow whose transition names differ from status names

## Claim

`JiraDataCenterTransport.transition_issue_by_name(remote_id, target_status)` matches the requested
name against each transition's **own name**, but every production caller passes a **destination
STATUS name**. On Jira's classic workflow those differ, so the lookup misses, the transport raises
`ValueError`, the applier SOFT-FAILS it into `bridge_alerts`, and the pass exits 0 having silently
not applied the status change.

## Evidence — measured live, not inferred

Harness run 30724309686 (job "jira DC harness smoke", main @ 216ceb830),
`test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]`:

    outbound status did not reach DC: fields.status.name is 'To Do'
    assert 'To Do' == 'In Progress'

and from the same run, the transport's own error text naming what the instance actually offers:

    no transition named 'In Progress' is available for RBJSAHY-1
    (available: ['Done', 'Start Progress'])

So the instance offers transitions **`Done`** and **`Start Progress`**. The reconciler asks for
`"In Progress"` — the value `jira_family.value_maps.LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` maps local `in_progress`
to — and that is a STATUS name, not a transition name.

## The mechanism, end to end

1. `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA["in_progress"] == "In Progress"` — a destination STATUS name. Correct: the
   map is documented as "Local status string -> Jira workflow state name".
2. The outbound path passes that value to `transition_issue_by_name`.
3. `transport.py`'s implementation does
   `next(t for t in transitions if t.get("name") == target_status)` — comparing against the
   TRANSITION's name.
4. No match -> `ValueError("no transition named ...")`.
5. `apply_handlers.record_backstop_failure` catches it, appends a `mutation-error` to
   `bridge_alerts`, logs a WARNING, and returns `soft_failed=True` so the pass continues.
6. The pass exits 0 with no traceback. The issue's status is unchanged.

## Why this is a silent PARTIAL failure, which is worse than a loud one

`Done` is BOTH a transition name and a status name on the classic workflow, so `closed -> "Done"`
happens to work. `in_progress -> "In Progress"` does not. **Some statuses sync and others silently
do not**, which reads as a flaky or partial bridge rather than a mapping defect.

## Why it was invisible until now

The DIG (Cloud) workflow evidently names its transitions after their destinations, so the two
spellings coincide there and the bug never fires. This is the same shape as every other defect this
epic found: an assumption that a Cloud-shaped instance's conventions hold on a DC-shaped one. The
existing live test `test_create_get_update_transition_roundtrip` PASSES precisely because it was
written to avoid the trap — its comment says so explicitly ("A transition's NAME is not its
destination STATUS name ... Asserting the status equals the transition name therefore fails against
a real instance") and it drives by a name read from the payload. The transport contract was never
adjusted to match that insight.

## Remediation

`transition_issue_by_name` should resolve a requested name against the transition's DESTINATION
STATUS as well as its own name — the transitions payload declares it in `to.name`. Prefer an exact
transition-name match first (preserving today's behaviour for callers that genuinely pass one),
then fall back to a unique `to.name` match; raise if the destination is ambiguous rather than
guessing. The error message must keep listing what IS available, and should list both spellings.

Do NOT "fix" this by changing `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` to hold transition names: that map is shared
with the inbound direction and with `config.local_to_jira_status`, it is documented as holding
workflow STATE names, and transition names are per-workflow so no single set would be correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `transition_issue_by_name` moves an issue to a requested DESTINATION STATUS on a workflow
      whose transition names differ from status names, asserted against a real instance
- [ ] an exact TRANSITION-name match still works unchanged (the existing live round-trip test
      passes with no edit), so this is additive rather than a behaviour swap
- [ ] an ambiguous destination (two transitions declaring the same `to.name`) RAISES naming the
      ambiguity rather than silently picking one
- [ ] an unresolvable name still raises, and the message lists the available transition names AND
      their destination statuses
- [ ] `test_outbound_mutation_round_trips[04-transition-status]` passes on the DC harness
- [ ] a unit test drives the classic-workflow shape (`Start Progress` -> `In Progress`) against a
      fake transitions payload, so the fix is pinned without needing the harness
data.title: Outbound status silently fails when transition names differ from status names
